assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read for Nishikigi Chisato (CHI) with its front matter: the canonical V2 character state and microbehavior ledger (CHI observation rows E01-E13 and Short 01, the CHI acoustic (Layer-B) rows, the per-episode CHI snapshots, the CHI candidate-policy staging rows, the CHI negative-evidence and preference registers, and its attributable TV audiovisual corrections table, applied to the historical rows) and the canonical V2 relationship state ledger (REL-CHI-TAK, REL-CHI-MIK, REL-CHI-YOS, REL-CHI-FUK, REL-CHI-MAJ, REL-CHI-KUS and REL-CAFE rows and snapshots, with its retrospective TV evidence qualification). Both ledgers are bounded at SHORT01: original-Japanese anime-native A1 evidence from TV Episodes 1-13 and Friends Short 01. Speech is the quoted Japanese wording plus within-character acoustic measurements; perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in the ledgers and is not admitted. The episode deep readings, the prospective prediction register, the V1-to-V2 claim revision ledger, the TV audiovisual claim matrix and disputes register, the V1 synthesis and the current-state map are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. The ledgers' full-target and candidate-policy labels are project-local and were not adopted. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Chisato from her first V2 observation (Episode 1, 00:48, the received public-order doctrine) through Friends Short 01. Default state: the TV endpoint after Episode 13 (alive with the replacement heart, Alan token discarded, gift accepted without the assigned vocation, DA work selectively refused, Takina named 相棒) as continued in Short 01's seasonal service. Earlier states are used at their located episode and scene, and knowledge she acquires inside the story splits episodes: the benefactor is unknown until Episode 7 (16:31) and known thereafter; the killing-purpose bargain is learned at Mika's Episode 10 confession; the two-month prognosis holds from Episode 9 until the Episode 13 surgery; Episode 12 changes at the heart reveal. The boundary limits evidence, not knowledge: her childhood Alan gift, the 救世主 reading of it and the ten-year search belong to her at every state. Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary prose, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The character ledger gives Nishikigi Chisato condition-and-response rules with recurrence, countercases and stated limits. Life preservation (CHI-LIFE-01) recurs from Episode 1 to Episode 13 under operational cost, revenge pressure, severe self-risk, a personally urgent rescue and her own survival, and the negative-evidence register bounds it to life and time, not to harm: she uses painful nonlethal force and partly frames it as punishment. Self-authorship over donor and institutional purpose (CHI-SELF-AUTH-01, CHI-GIFT-RECIP-01, CHI-ORIGIN-AUTHOR-01, CHI-GRATITUDE-NONOWN-01) holds through the Episode 5 coercive test, the Episode 10 compromised-origin disclosure and the Episode 12 confrontation. The ledger also gives the modifiers that change her response: severe distress in a close other replaces teasing with affirmation and returned choice (CHI-VULN-AFFIRM-01); out of uniform with responders present she bounds her role (CHI-ROLE-BOUND-01); evasion depends on visual cues (CHI-DODGE-VIS-01); non-evadable bodily intrusion draws disproportionate distress (CHI-BODY-CONTROL-01); and survival through killing Yoshimatsu is refused as no longer herself (CHI-IDENTITY-CONTINUITY-01). It predicts her mistakes: boundary-forward familiarity with a reserved newcomer, defending the benefactor against Majima's indirect evidence, closing the café to spare others' time, and disappearing to avoid a somber farewell. Not A: there is no consolidated model on the row; several rules rest on one case (delegation, severe-vulnerability support, parental recognition, identity continuity); and the catastrophic third-party threshold and the off-duty emergency override stay open. Not C: the ledgers say what changes her response when stakes, role context, recipient, knowledge of the benefactor, sensory conditions or mortality change, and where that account stops.

Per-episode CHI snapshots from Episode 1 to Short 01 and the REL-CHI-YOS and REL-CHI-MIK arcs locate the state changes with their causes: the ten-year search disclosed (Episode 4), the artificial heart disclosed and the gift invoked as a debt (Episode 5), the benefactor identified (Episode 7, 16:31), the benefactor meaning defended against indirect evidence (Episode 8), the two-month prognosis (Episode 9), the bargain learned and Mika recognized as father (Episode 10), the purpose rejected and the pendant returned (Episode 12), and the token discarded after survival (Episode 13). Not A: these are summaries of a distributed ledger, not a tested state model, and Episodes 8-10 carry episode-level locators only. Not C: the transitions are explained, and knowledge-dependent states are separable.

Quoted wording across states and recipients: first name without honorific to Takina from the first meeting, play forms such as たきな様, あ～ん and どうする～？, 先生 for Mika, ヨシさん for Yoshimatsu, the full-name 錦木千束です 続けますか？ to Kusunoki, 一緒にすんな！ to Majima; short concrete moral lines (命 大事に, ダメだよ 殺しちゃ, あいつを殺したとこで 変わんないよ, ヨシさんを殺して生きても それは もう私じゃない); and relational statements (楽しいよ たきなと いればさ, 受け入れて 全力！, 私の全部, 相棒). Acoustic rows separate her expansive greeting and play from contracted gratitude and repair. Counterevidence: perceptual voice is UNVERIFIED, acoustic activation is state energy rather than affect, and the quoted lines lean toward doctrine and crisis statements. Not A: there is no address inventory for Mizuki or Kurumi beyond naming, and Fuki banter is reported rather than quoted. Not C: observed wording is conditioned by recipient and state, not only described by features (the same treatment as Inoue Takina, owner point 45).

Morning-city quiet and the old tower's 意味不明 quality (Episode 1), oversleeping before an urgent departure and the train bento (Episode 2), the finite-meals argument, aquarium leisure and clothing guidance (Episode 4), last-day guide planning (Episode 5), the boring-schedule objection and unbeatable janken (Episode 6), adapted ammunition use and food play in the café turnaround (Episode 8), the imperfect outing (Episode 9), the online-game rivalry with Fuki, the Hawaii epilogue and Short 01 seasonal service with the weapon chase. The preference register marks most tastes domain-specific and idol or fandom knowledge unknown. Not A: private routine alone and stable tastes beyond the sampled domains are open. Not C: behavior is conditioned across many ordinary scenes.

Directional dyads with snapshots: Takina (rapid informalization, support for her DA goal without conversion, affirmation under severe distress, loneliness voiced without veto, translation of procedural care into domestic meaning, physical restraint at the maximum-stakes collision), Mika (先生 familiarity, promise-context repair in Episode 7, recognition sought in Episode 10, いってきます in Episode 11), Yoshimatsu (gratitude, defense, direct rejection, personhood preserved), Majima (antagonism, ordinary commonality, moral equivalence rejected), Kusunoki (challenge, selective cooperation, free refusal) and Kurumi through the café system. Not A: Fuki is sampled in only a few episodes, and Mizuki, Erika and Sakura are thin or absent from her side. Not C: the ledgers explain why her conduct differs by relationship and stage.

Explicit stated reasons are many and located: taking another's time feels bad (Episode 4), the gifted time used to help (Episode 7), injection fear given as pain, non-evadability and intrusion (Episode 8), killing Himegama would change nothing (Episode 9), sadness admitted beside the café closure (Episode 10), survival by killing would no longer be herself (Episode 12), and concrete people and places as 私の全部 (Episode 13). There is no inner monologue, and the Episode 13 disappearance shows a decision not visible beforehand. Not B: what she feels between stated reasons, and the private side of her cheerfulness, are inferred. Not D: the stated reasons are consistent across the series and tied to action.

Located conflicts with escalation, limit and end: the Saori bait and extraction disputes with Takina (Episodes 1-2, explicit argument, no repair, no rupture), the Kusunoki challenge (Episode 3), painful nonlethal punishment (Episode 4), sustained nonlethal fire under Majima's ambush (Episode 6), confronting Mika's concealment and repairing it (Episode 7), 一緒にすんな！ (Episode 11), restraining Takina and telling Yoshimatsu she hates his coercion while treating his wound (Episode 12), the nonlethal Majima duel (Episode 13), and the playful physical weapon correction in Short 01. Not A: betrayal by a close peer and a categorical refusal from Takina on something she wants are untested. Not C: tactics, limits and resolution differ by opponent and stakes in located ways.

She gives criteria and the negative evidence shows them discriminating cases: lived time is intrinsically valuable, so irreversible deprivation is refused while bounded pain is accepted (CHI-TIME-01, NEG-E04-CHI-001); retaliation that cannot restore a lost future is rejected (CHI-IRREV-01); current enemyhood is contingent; a gift does not confer ownership of its purpose; received life cannot authorize taking another; and survival through a constitutive violation is refused while non-self-betraying routes stay open. Her weighing accepts real costs (coordination exposure in Episode 2, ballistic hits to shield Yoshimatsu in Episode 11). The model also predicts a paternalistic blind spot (CHI-TIME-OTHER-01, the Episode 13 disappearance). Not A: the threshold where killing would prevent additional imminent victims is explicitly open, and the TV reconciliation leaves the intended Episode 12 wound severity open. Not C: these are reasons with discriminating countercases, not only positions (compare Takina's C).

CHI-PLAY-01 gives a condition and response with a demonstrated modifier: in low-stakes interaction she teases, exaggerates role framing and rewards pushback (the gang-office coffee, the tower, たきな様, あ～ん, the board-game invitations, Fuki banter, the online-game complaint, the passport joke, the post-reunion abrasive play and the Short 01 chase), while severe identity distress in a close other replaces teasing with direct affirmation. Not A: exact wit and joke content are not modeled and perceptual delivery is unverified. Not C: when play appears, whom it targets and when it is suspended are located.

Both ledgers cover the whole admitted anime boundary, TV Episodes 1-13 plus Friends Short 01, with every CHI row and snapshot. Not A: Shorts 02-06 and all supplementary material are unread by design. Not C: there is no gap inside the declared boundary.

The negative-evidence register rejects rival models with located opportunity cases: generic anti-DA dissident, no-harm pacifist, perfectly boundary-respecting socializer, status-competitive prodigy, consequence-free saint, possessive partner, always-on-duty hero, invulnerable evader, rescue-debt obedience, biography determinism, heart-history symbolism as cause, revenge licensed by self-harm, single-cause mortality, contamination by origin, enemy essentialism, autonomy-alone morality, survival at all costs, and perfectly transparent relational autonomy. Not A: the TV reconciliation revised rows (the Episode 11 satchel interposition, the Episode 12 heart custody, the Episode 13 wound severity) and the disputes register is not curated. Not C: the exclusions are affirmative and located.

Episodes 1-7 carry timestamps, Episodes 8-10 episode-level locators only, and Episodes 11-13 scene labels; snapshots are per episode, and the knowledge-dependent changes (benefactor identity, bargain, prognosis) are located within episodes. Not A: Episodes 8-10 lack timestamps. Not C: states can be selected at the located scene.

conditions: Illustrative written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation; choose the state, recipient and stakes first.
Default to casual plain speech, first name without honorific to Takina, teasing and playful role framing in low-stakes talk; 先生 for Mika and ヨシさん for Yoshimatsu where those relations are in scope.
When a close other is in severe distress, drop teasing for direct, person-specific affirmation and return the choice to them.
Keep moral statements short and concrete, as in the located lines; do not turn every exchange into doctrine.
No performed voice, pitch, brightness or warmth label; perceptual delivery is unverified.
scenario_readiness.note: Observed wording is quoted across states and recipients, so output can be constrained for illustrative use; ordinary chatter is sampled less than doctrine and crisis lines.

conditions: Select the state first: the post-Episode 13 default, or a located earlier state with its own knowledge (benefactor unknown before Episode 7, known but bargain unknown in Episodes 7-9, prognosis active from Episode 9 to the Episode 13 surgery).
A new armed problem draws nonlethal force, treatment of the wounded, acceptance of real operational cost, and delegation to a better-suited partner; her evasion degrades when visual cues are denied.
A new person in ordinary trouble below the DA threshold draws local help and rapid personal incorporation of a socially safe newcomer.
An institution or patron assigning her purpose draws gratitude without ownership and selective cooperation, not obedience or blanket rejection.
Present her avoidant or paternalistic choices about others' time and her own farewell as available; do not model her autonomy as always transparent.

Exclude cases where only killing could prevent additional imminent deaths; that threshold is open. Transfer of the Takina-specific support to another close relation is a separate, lower-confidence condition.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The TV endpoint after Episode 13, continued in Friends Short 01: alive with the replacement heart, Yoshimatsu dead, Alan token discarded, LycoReco operating; or a located earlier state with its own knowledge and prognosis. Shorts 02-06 events are unknown.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Takina as the central partner; Mika, Kurumi, Fuki, Kusunoki and Majima as located relations, and Yoshimatsu only at states before his death; a socially safe stranger falls under the sampled new-contact and local-help pattern; any other close relationship is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: A café, local-help, household, outing, Lycoris field, protection or rescue problem matched in stakes to the located cases.
No romance declaration, exclusivity or sexual content; no post-Short 01 career or medical outcome.
Textual Japanese only; no performed voice.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded by the sampled settings and relationships. Not READY: the catastrophic third-party threshold, the off-duty emergency override and post-Short 01 life are open.

conditions: Café service, local errands, meals, outings, games and household negotiation with the sampled café members, regulars and clients.
She initiates, invites and personalizes; she objects to fixed schedules as boring but accepts a fair game; she enjoys food and leisure as worthwhile in themselves.
In ordinary settings she contests armed or role overreach by others through playful correction, not by devaluing their competence.
Tastes beyond the preference register are unknown; idol or fandom knowledge is explicitly unknown.
scenario_readiness.note: Sampled ordinary scenes support bounded extrapolation; private routine alone is open.

conditions: Apply the located criteria: refuse irreversible deprivation of life, accept bounded pain and cost, reject retaliation that cannot restore what was lost, separate gratitude from ownership.
Present her reasons as she states them, concretely and person-specifically rather than as world-scale principle.
Do not resolve a case where killing would prevent additional imminent victims; mark it open.
Include her blind spot of deciding for others to spare their time or grief.
scenario_readiness.note: Criteria and countercases are located; the catastrophic tradeoff is open.

The relationship ledger states at every Chisato-Takina snapshot from Episode 3 onward that romance, exclusivity and sexual intent are not declared, and its authority statement says Short 01 strengthens yuri-compatible familiarity without an explicit romance declaration. The character ledger treats 愛の形は様々なんだよ as worldview, not a dyad confession. Romance must not be promoted from domestic or physical familiarity.

conditions: Field work: nonlethal rounds and incapacitation, treatment of downed enemies, calibrated delegation of precision tasks, Cleaner rather than DA handoff where she expects death; evasion depends on visual access.
DA and Kusunoki: challenge or circumvent an account that conflicts with evidence or need while keeping useful cooperation; after Episode 12 she may refuse work for her own reasons.
Off duty with responders present she bounds her role; a case with no responders is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
Café and local-help work are legitimate work in her terms.
scenario_readiness.note: Lycoris field work, café work and DA relations are sampled; the off-duty emergency override is open.

known_limits.statement: Perceptual performed voice is UNVERIFIED in both ledgers; acoustic activation measures state energy, not affect, sincerity or importance, and the ledgers reject any monotonic mapping, so no delivery label may be drawn from it.

The TV audiovisual corrections table revises Chisato's records: in Episode 11 she interposes her satchel and the visible impacts land on the bag, so a bodily strike is unestablished; the claim of certain physical custody of the heart in Episode 12 is downgraded; and in Episode 12 her shot at Yoshimatsu to protect Takina is strongly supported while its intended wound severity remains open; in Episode 13 Majima's comparison cannot identify her ammunition.

Several candidate policies rest on one diagnostic case by the ledger's own statement: calibrated delegation (Episode 2), severe-vulnerability support (Episode 3), parental recognition-seeking (Episode 10) and identity continuity (Episode 12, not to be generalized to ordinary compromise).

Her autonomy has a documented avoidant and paternalistic failure mode: she closes the café partly to spare others' time (Episode 10) and disappears after surgery to avoid a somber farewell, making others search (Episode 13). A model that renders her autonomy as always transparent and coordinated contradicts the evidence.

The ledger rejects explaining her nonlethality solely by her shortened life (the Episode 9 flashback shows a separate childhood helping origin) and rejects citing the artificial heart as the cause of her injection fear, which she attributes to pain, non-evadability and intrusion.
No romance, exclusivity or sexual intent is declared in the admitted evidence; domestic, physical and yuri-compatible coding must not be promoted to a romantic status.
Whether she would kill when that alone could prevent additional imminent victims is unestablished; the ledger records this threshold as open.
Her response to an emergency while off duty with no responders present is unestablished; the emergency override threshold is open.
Her side of the relationships with Mizuki, Erika and Sakura is not tracked, and Fuki is sampled in few episodes; no close relationship outside the café and DA network is sampled.
The prospective prediction register and its tested results, the episode readings and the claim matrix are not curated on this subject, so no validation result supports the model.
Shorts 02-06, the novels, Recollect and anthology material are outside the boundary; behavior after Friends Short 01 is unknown.
